summary: Supplier invoice held in AP due to handwritten VAT correction captured incorrectly by OCR
description:
Issue summary:
A vendor-sent PDF invoice (vendor ID VND-78421) contains a handwritten correction to the VAT line (originally 20% crossed out and replaced with 19%). The OCR pipeline ingested the PDF and captured the VAT amount as if it were 20%, which caused the automated 3-way match and tax validation rules to flag the invoice and place it on hold.

Impact:
- Single invoice on payment run hold (payment due next week) affecting vendor relationship for EU regional supplier.
- Manual intervention required to approve/override, delaying AP throughput.
- Potential tax reporting mismatch if paid with incorrect VAT.

Environment:
- AP automation pipeline (prod) feeding into payments export (SEPA) for eu-west region.
- OCR pipeline v2.3.1 running on inference-ocr cluster.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Upload invoice_78421_scans.pdf to AP intake bucket.
2) OCR pipeline extracts fields into ocr_extract_78421.json.
3) AP validation service compares VAT percentage against PO/line-item expectations.
4) Validation rules detect mismatch and set invoice status to "Hold: VAT mismatch".

Observed behavior:
- OCR captured VAT rate as 20% and VAT amount of 240.00 EUR.
- The invoice header shows handwritten correction to 19% and VAT 228.00 EUR (handwritten adjacent to typed line).
- AP service flagged as discrepancy and blocked payment export.

Expected behavior:
- OCR or downstream validation should surface the handwritten override as a low-confidence field and attach an image snippet for manual review rather than auto-hold without context.

Initial logs and artifacts:
- ocr_extract_78421.json shows vat_rate: "20%", vat_amount: "240.00" with confidence 0.88 for the typed field and a separate detected annotation with confidence 0.42 for handwritten text.
- AP validation log: "VAT_MISMATCH: expected 19% per vendor contract; detected 20% from OCR; hold applied."
- S3 object paths: s3://ap-intake/2026-03-09/invoice_78421_scans.pdf

Notes on vendor/contract:
- Vendor VND-78421 has a standing contract specifying 19% VAT for these services (contract in Confluence link above). PO-55233 attached to invoice expects 19% VAT.

Requested immediate action:
- Allow manual override path for this invoice with an explicit flag and audit trail so AP can release payment while preserving evidence for tax reporting.
- Backend: improve OCR/validation to attach low-confidence handwritten detections as evidence instead of auto-hold where contract/PO suggests the lower rate.
investigation_notes: 03-10: Triage by AP automation. Confirmed invoice present in intake and flagged by validation rule. 03-11: OCR team inspected ocr_extract_78421.json; found separate handwritten annotation detected with low confidence. 03-11: Hypothesis - current rule treats any mismatch between OCR-detected fields and PO as immediate hold without examining alternative low-confidence detections or vendor contract metadata. 03-12: Ran a synthetic test with similar handwritten corrections; pipeline consistently prefers higher-confidence typed value and does not escalate handwritten snippets for manual review. 03-12: Finance ops confirms vendor contract and PO both indicate 19% VAT.
workaround_and_resolution_plan:
Workaround: AP can perform a manual override for INT-410222 using the 'AP Manual Review' console: attach scanned invoice, set 'verified_vat' to 19% and add comment referencing vendor contract. This will allow the next SEPA export to include the invoice.
Short-term resolution (next 3 business days): add an intermediate 'LowConfidenceAnnotation' review step to validation to flag but not auto-hold when a low-confidence handwritten detection contradicts typed OCR and PO/contract indicates a specific tax rate.
Medium-term resolution (2-4 weeks): update OCR post-processing to: 1) surface all detected annotations with confidence scores in AP UI; 2) add rule to prefer contract/PO VAT when detected handwritten correction has confidence >= 0.35 and typed field confidence < 0.9; 3) add telemetry/metric for handwritten overrides for further tuning.
Owners: AP Automation (Lucas Chen) + OCR team (Priya Rao).
